body:
## Summary
Every CLI test in this context builds its own tempdir + redirect harness and parses the process output its own way — whole-stdout `json.loads`, strict last line, or last non-blank stderr line — and none of them reads it the way `app/_lib/python-runner.ts` does. Replace the eight open-coded harnesses with one `run_cli` in `_helpers.py` whose readers are ports of `parsePythonJson` and `parseStderrError`, pinned to the real TS functions by one shared case table that both languages run.

## Description
The CLIs exist to be read by one program: the Next bridge. Its reader scans stdout backwards for the last JSON object (skipping trailing interpreter chatter and bare scalars) and takes the envelope from the last non-empty stderr line, deriving a code from status and exit 2. The Python tests assert on a different reader. `test_match_cli.py:64` parses the whole of stdout and turns an empty stdout into `{}`; `test_winnability.py:534` and `test_agentfit.py:188` take the strict last line; `test_group_compare_cli.py` re-parses the envelope inline three times. The result is stricter than production in one place (a harmless trailing warning goes red) and looser in another (a silent empty stdout reads as `{}`). The envelope contract gets checked unevenly too: only `test_winnability.py:624-635` asserts the emitted code is in `_cli.ERROR_CODES`, and `test_match_cli.py:182-186` pins reasoning_cli's not-found path by exit code and English message alone, so that path could fall back to an uncoded 500 and the tests would stay green.

The move: `_helpers.run_cli(main, argv, files=...) -> CliRun(code, payload, envelope, stdout, stderr)` writes the input files, captures both streams, and reads them through `read_stdout_payload` / `read_stderr_envelope`, which port the TS readers line for line. `CliRun` also checks the envelope vocabulary by default. A JSON case table, `pipeline/jobfit/tests/fixtures/bridge_read_cases.json`, gives stdout, stderr and exit code with the expected read. `test_bridge_reader.py` runs it through the port, and `app/_lib/python-runner-bridge-cases.test.ts` runs it through the real TS functions, so the port cannot drift from the reader it stands for. The five CLI test files then migrate onto the harness. Each keeps its assertions and drops its scaffolding.

## Flow
1. Author the case table (≈12 rows: trailing noise, scalar-only, empty, pre-result warning, envelope with/without/blank code, plain-text stderr at exit 1 and 2). 2. TS test: feed each row to `parsePythonJson`/`parseStderrError`, compare to `expect`. 3. Python port + `run_cli` + `test_bridge_reader.py` over the same rows. 4. Migrate test_match_cli (and add the not_found code assertion), test_matrix_cli, test_group_compare_cli, test_winnability, test_agentfit — mock-patched provider/ledger cases keep their own `mock.patch` context around `run_cli`. 5. Gate.

## Expected impact
All five CLI suites in the Match / Fit Matrix / group-eval / winnability / agent-fit lane assert what the bridge will actually hand to the route, and every coded envelope has its vocabulary checked without anyone having to remember. About 8 harness copies (roughly 150 lines) collapse into one helper. The next CLI test gets bridge fidelity at no extra cost, and the other ~30 suite files that redirect stdio (grep count) have a shape to migrate to later.

## Evaluation
Claim: the CLI tests read process output through a port of the bridge's reader, pinned to the TS original by a shared case table.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass.
After: 8 of 8.
Method: gate — `npm run test:python:gate` (test_bridge_reader + the five migrated files) and `npm run test:unit` (python-runner-bridge-cases.test.ts); the case table rows are the oracle for both.
Result: pending build.
Gate: none.

body:
## Summary
Czech gender parity has three consumers of hand-authored surfaces. Two are machine-checked: taxonomy terms and adjacent_domain_signals, both derived at load and scanned by `scan_gender_gaps`. The third, `transferable._TRANSFERABLE_MAP`, is held only by a comment and a hand list of pairs. Measured today: a woman whose CV title is the standard feminine 'Právnice' loses three transferable meta-skills ('analytical thinking', 'attention to detail', 'negotiation') that 'Právník' and 'Právnička' both earn. The fix is to derive the map's feminine forms the way the taxonomy derives its own, and to make the scan read the map, so that a masculine-only signal can no longer be written.

## Description
`transferable.py:18-27` states the rule in prose ('any new Czech signal added here must be checked the same way') and meets it by hand with the stems 'pedagož', 'právnič', 'vojačk' and 'poradkyn'. The hand-picked stem 'právnič' covers 'Právnička' and misses 'Právnice', the dictionary-standard feminine. `taxonomy_check.scan_gender_gaps` (:455-496) would find that gap at once. `feminine_probe_forms('právník')` returns ('právnice', 'právnička') and the authored map reaches only the second. The scan still never sees it, because it covers terms and adjacent_domain_signals and nothing else. The tests in this context pin the pairs someone thought to list (`GENDERED_TITLES`, `ROLE_TITLES`). The class is closed by the scanner, and the hand lists cannot close it.

The move: split the map into an authored table and a load-time expansion that adds each Czech signal's full feminine word forms from `taxonomy.feminine_probe_forms`. It deliberately uses the full words and not the `feminine_variants` stems. The map is matched by raw substring, and the stem 'právnic' would false-credit every accountant whose CV says 'právnických osob'. Acceptance case 2 is the negative control for that. `scan_gender_gaps` gains the map as a third consumer, which mirrors `map_transferable`'s substring rule the same way it already mirrors `domain_distance`'s. `main()` reports it. The now-derivable hand stems leave the authored table. 'poradkyn' stays, with its reason stated, because the probe vocabulary has no -ce→-kyně rule.

## Flow
1. Tests first: the Právnice case, the právnických negative control, the planted-signal scan, the English no-op. 2. transferable.py: `_AUTHORED_TRANSFERABLE_MAP` + `_with_feminine_forms()` → `_TRANSFERABLE_MAP`; drop 'pedagož'/'právnič'/'vojačk'. 3. taxonomy_check.py: scan the authored map (derive flag mirrors the existing one), wire into `main()`. 4. Doc: docs/features/matching/README.md gender-parity paragraph names the third consumer. 5. Gate.

## Expected impact
The same career now earns the same transferable credit whichever grammatical gender the CV is written in. That credit feeds `build_match_candidate` (skills credited `professional`), `compute_potential` and the `transferable_strengths` soft signal. Later map edits are covered by the gate that already covers the taxonomy's own Czech vocabulary, and no longer depend on a reviewer remembering a comment.

## Evaluation
Claim: every Czech agent-noun signal in the transferable map reaches its feminine forms by derivation, and the gender scan fails on one that does not.
Before: 0 of 7 acceptance cases pass.
After: 7 of 7.
Method: gate — `npm run test:python:gate` (test_transferable_gender, test_taxonomy_gender, test_taxonomy_check incl. `test_cli_exits_clean`, test_transferable, test_soft_signals).
Result: pending build.
Gate: contract.
